result.text: Title: Work and Live in Austria Please check the requirements for working and living in austria.
Create a process that assists you for a combination of the steps.

Include: * Organizing accomodation and bank account (negotiation) * Visa (every x amount of months) - Rot-Weiss-Rot Card Requirements General principles and requirements for the issue of Visas: * visa application form * a travel document valid in Austria, with a validity period exceeding the duration of the visa by at least three months and with at least two empty pages, that was issued within the last ten years * a passport photo (portrait format, 35 x 45 mm) in accordance with the specified passport photo criteria * presentation of an fully comprehensive travel health insurance policy for the planned duration of the stay (amount of cover: 30.000 Euro, valid for the entire Schengen area) * proof of sufficient means of subsistence for the duration of the intended stay and for the return journey to the country of origin or residence * other evidence requested by the relevant authorities (hotel reservations, invitations, booking confirmations, return flight ticket, proof of gainful employment etc.) - as these are adapted to local standards and coordinated with other Schengen representations, the evidence to be provided may vary depending on location * absence of other grounds for refusal (residence prohibition, alert issued by a Schengen country) Depending on the circumstances, additional documents may be requested.
Please contact the representation in advance for more information.

Generally speaking, all visa types are issued by representation offices (→ BMEIA) abroad or, in specific exceptional cases, by certain border control posts or, where extension of the visa is permitted, by the state police headquarters.
Schengen visas must be issued by the representation office of the country in which the main travel destination of the visa applicant is located.

If the applicant intends to spend an equal amount of time in several countries (for example, when touring), the competent representation office is that of the country in whose territory the main travel destination is located, on the basis of the length and purpose of the stay.
If it is not possible to determine a main travel destination, the member country of first entry into the Schengen area is responsible for issuing the visa.
Territorial competence for applications for category A and C visas falls to the representation office in the consular district where the legal place of residence of the applicant is located.

A representation office may claim exceptional competence for applications from third‑country nationals legally residing but not registered in their district if the applicant can provide justification as to why they had to submit their application to that particular consulate.
Type D visas, however, must be applied for at the competent Austrian representation.
The provisions of Section 8 of the FPG apply to type D visas.

In accordance with these provisions, the territorial competence for carrying out official actions in relation to visas is determined on the basis of the foreign national's the place of residence (i.e.
their centre of interest, verifiable by means of e.g.
registration forms, residence permit, visa).

A list of all representation offices (addresses, telephone numbers, opening hours, special requirements for issuing visas etc.) can be found on the website of the Federal Ministry of European and International Affairs.

result.rule: When the description lists several items or conditions that a request must satisfy before it can be decided, gives no order between them, and some of them are to be checked by a system or an external institution while others must be supplied by the applicant: Model each listed item or condition as its own activity, keeping the description's wording, in a parallel split placed after the common starting point. Model items checked by a system or an external institution as service or manual activities in their own branch, and items the applicant must supply as user activities. When the description says an item must be obtained or renewed if it does not meet a stated condition, add an explicit activity for obtaining it on that route. Join all branches with a parallel gateway before the decision or the next step, so the next step waits for every item. Do not merge the items into one combined activity and do not chain them in sequence.

When the description lists two or more actions that must all be carried out after a common point, with no order or alternative stated between them, and only then leads to a later step: Model a parallel gateway that splits into one task per listed action, keeping each action as its own task with the description's wording, in a separate branch. Join all branches with a parallel gateway before the later step, so the later step waits for every action. Do not chain the actions in sequence, do not use an exclusive gateway for them, and do not leave any branch without a connecting flow to the join.

When the description states that one item is subjected to several named checks or assessments, each with its own stated aim, and gives no order between them: Model each named check or assessment as its own task, keeping the description's wording for it, and place these tasks in a parallel split after the common starting point. Do not merge them into one combined task. Join all branches with a parallel gateway before the next step that needs all of the results.

When the description lists two or more activities that are performed without a stated order and must all be completed before a later step begins: Model a parallel gateway that splits into one outgoing branch per listed activity, and a parallel gateway that joins those branches before the next step. Do not chain the activities in sequence, and do not use an exclusive gateway for them.

result.process_description:
Title: Work and Live in Austria

Please check the requirements for working and living in austria.
Create a process that assists you for a combination of the steps.

Include:
* Organizing accomodation and bank account (negotiation)
* Visa (every x amount of months) - Rot-Weiss-Rot Card  

Requirements  
General principles and requirements for the issue of Visas:  
* visa application form 
* a travel document valid in Austria, with a validity period exceeding the duration of the visa by at least three months and with at least two empty pages, that was issued within the last ten years 
* a passport photo (portrait format, 35 x 45 mm) in accordance with the specified passport photo criteria 
* presentation of an fully comprehensive travel health insurance policy for the planned duration of the stay (amount of cover: 30.000 Euro, valid for the entire Schengen area) 
* proof of sufficient means of subsistence for the duration of the intended stay and for the return journey to the country of origin or residence 
* other evidence requested by the relevant authorities (hotel reservations, invitations, booking confirmations, return flight ticket, proof of gainful employment etc.) - as these are adapted to local standards and coordinated with other Schengen representations, the evidence to be provided may vary depending on location 
* absence of other grounds for refusal (residence prohibition, alert issued by a Schengen country)  

Depending on the circumstances, additional documents may be requested.
Please contact the representation in advance for more information.

Generally speaking, all visa types are issued by representation offices (→ BMEIA) abroad or, in specific exceptional cases, by certain border control posts or, where extension of the visa is permitted, by the state police headquarters.

Schengen visas must be issued by the representation office of the country in which the main travel destination of the visa applicant is located.
If the applicant intends to spend an equal amount of time in several countries (for example, when touring), the competent representation office is that of the country in whose territory the main travel destination is located, on the basis of the length and purpose of the stay.
If it is not possible to determine a main travel destination, the member country of first entry into the Schengen area is responsible for issuing the visa.

Territorial competence for applications for category A and C visas falls to the representation office in the consular district where the legal place of residence of the applicant is located.
A representation office may claim exceptional competence for applications from third‑country nationals legally residing but not registered in their district if the applicant can provide justification as to why they had to submit their application to that particular consulate.

Type D visas, however, must be applied for at the competent Austrian representation.
The provisions of Section 8 of the FPG apply to type D visas.
In accordance with these provisions, the territorial competence for carrying out official actions in relation to visas is determined on the basis of the foreign national's the place of residence (i.e. their centre of interest, verifiable by means of e.g. registration forms, residence permit, visa).

A list of all representation offices (addresses, telephone numbers, opening hours, special requirements for issuing visas etc.) can be found on the website of the Federal Ministry of European and International Affairs.

result.rule: When the description lists several items or conditions that a request must satisfy before it can be decided, gives no order between them, and some of them are to be checked by a system or an external institution while others must be supplied by the applicant: Model each listed item or condition as its own activity, keeping the description's wording, in a parallel split placed after the common starting point. Model items checked by a system or an external institution as service or manual activities in their own branch, and items the applicant must supply as user activities. When the description says an item must be obtained or renewed if it does not meet a stated condition, add an explicit activity for obtaining it on that route. Join all branches with a parallel gateway before the decision or the next step, so the next step waits for every item. Do not merge the items into one combined activity and do not chain them in sequence.

When the description states that a participant has an obligation to report or submit an item again and again within a cycle, and a later statement says that a condition ends or continues that obligation: Model each such recurring report or submission as a user task that the participant performs inside the cycle, placed before a gateway that decides whether the cycle repeats. Base that gateway on the condition the description gives for continuing or ending the obligation. Do not represent the reporting only as a gateway, a timer, or a flow condition, and do not drop it when the description also gives a separate condition that changes what happens afterwards.

When the description states that one assessment step in a sentence covers several named criteria of different kinds (a check and an evaluation), listed in a stated order, and a later decision depends on the result: Model each named criterion as its own bpmn:task, using the description's wording for each, placed in sequence in the order the description states them, before the decision that depends on the assessment. Do not merge the criteria into one task whose label lists them all, and do not drop any stated criterion.

When the description states one user action whose clause joins several distinct inputs or choices with 'and' (for example, 'provides X and Y' or 'selects A, B, and C'), followed by a further step that depends on them: Model each distinct input or choice named in that clause as its own user task, in the order the description states them, and connect these tasks in sequence before the task for the dependent step. Do not merge the items into one task, and do not leave any stated item out of the model.
